title: Preparing a Hybrid Tea, Floribunda or Grandiflora rose for winter

common.applies_to: Hybrid Tea, Floribunda or Grandiflora rose (a rose that has passed PKR-SGT-000003), in an area with hard winter frosts
common.preserved_uncertainty: Winter mounding applies where winters bring hard frosts (F9). Mound heights vary between sources, from 8 to 18 inches, around the common 10–12 (Source Register §3, matter 4). Collars and wraps rest on two sources and are described particularly for climbing roses or exposed sites (F10). All sources are from the US (ARC §5).

content.heading: Preparing for winter
content.label: If your winters bring hard frosts…

items.text: Once the rose has had hard frosts and gone dormant, mound soil, compost or mulch about 10–12 inches (25–30 cm) high around the base, covering the graft union (the swollen join near the base); one source says up to 18 inches (45 cm). Remove the mound in spring once hard frosts have passed.

In colder or more exposed spots, you can also wrap the canes in burlap or evergreen boughs. One source also builds a collar of tar paper or wire mesh around the rose and fills it with straw, pine bark or peat moss.
Water thoroughly after the first hard frost and before the ground freezes, and clear fallen leaves from around the plant before winter.

content.disclosure: This care advice comes mainly from US gardening services. Timings and amounts may differ where you live.
